AI.conclusion: The results validate a context-conditioned description of measurement backaction over proxy-only null models, demonstrating that higher-order context dependence is essential for characterizing measurement-induced disturbance in multiscale dynamic circuits.

title: Accelerated Rydberg-EIT quantum memory via shortcuts to adiabaticity
summary: Electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) enables coherent light-matter storage, forming the basis of photonic quantum memories that are essential for scalable quantum networks and distributed quantum computing. However, accelerating the storage process violates the adiabatic condition, resulting in the excitation of the lossy intermediate state and a reduction in writing efficiency. We propose and numerically investigate a high-speed, high-fidelity quantum storage scheme by incorporating a shortcut-to-adiabaticity (STA) technique based on counter-diabatic (CD) driving. By introducing a precisely engineered auxiliary field into a conventional EIT system, our protocol significantly shortens the writing time beyond the conventional adiabatic limit while effectively suppressing the transient population of the lossy intermediate state. Furthermore, our scheme demonstrates strong flexibility in pulse design, remaining effective across different temporal profiles of both the control and signal fields. It also exhibits robustness against imperfections in the CD drive. Even with imperfect single-photon writing and non-ideal Rydberg blockade, the scheme retains clear advantages, maintaining high storage performance and overcoming the intrinsic speed-fidelity trade-off of traditional EIT protocols. These features pave the way for fast and robust quantum devices suitable for high-throughput quantum repeaters and advanced quantum information processing.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a high-speed, high-fidelity quantum memory scheme using shortcut-to-adiabaticity techniques to overcome the speed-fidelity trade-off in conventional EIT-based quantum storage.
AI.motivation: Traditional EIT-based quantum memories face a fundamental speed-fidelity trade-off: accelerating storage violates adiabatic conditions, exciting lossy intermediate states and reducing efficiency. This limitation hinders high-throughput quantum networks and distributed quantum computing applications.
AI.method: The authors incorporate a shortcut-to-adiabaticity (STA) technique based on counter-diabatic (CD) driving into a conventional EIT system. They introduce a precisely engineered auxiliary field that enables fast storage beyond the adiabatic limit while suppressing transient population of lossy intermediate states.
AI.result: The proposed scheme significantly shortens writing time beyond conventional adiabatic limits while maintaining high fidelity. It demonstrates flexibility across different temporal profiles of control and signal fields, robustness against CD drive imperfections, and maintains advantages even with imperfect single-photon writing and non-ideal Rydberg blockade.
AI.conclusion: The STA-based quantum storage scheme overcomes the intrinsic speed-fidelity trade-off of traditional EIT protocols, enabling fast and robust quantum devices suitable for high-throughput quantum repeaters and advanced quantum information processing applications.

title: Learning Entanglement Quasiprobability from Noisy and Incomplete Data
comment: Yu-Zhuo Li and Li-Chao Peng contributed equally. Corresponding authors: Li-Chao Peng (plc@bit.edu.cn) and Ke-Mi Xu (xukemi@bit.edu.cn)
summary: Negativities in quasiprobability distributions, a foundational concept originating in quantum optics, serve as a fundamental signature of quantum nonclassicality, with entanglement quasiprobabilities offering a necessary and sufficient criterion for entanglement. However, practical reconstruction of entanglement quasiprobabilities conventionally requires full quantum state tomography, severely limiting scalability. Here, we propose a deep-learning framework that reconstructs entanglement quasiprobabilities directly from incomplete local projective measurements, bypassing full state reconstruction. Using a residual neural network, partial measurement outcomes are mapped to high-fidelity entanglement quasiprobabilities. Numerical benchmarks up to three qubits show more than a $30\times$ reduction in reconstruction error compared with state-of-the-art tomographic methods. Experimental validation on photonic entangled states demonstrates reconstruction and entanglement detection with substantially reduced measurement resources. Our results establish machine-learning-assisted reconstruction of entanglement quasiprobabilities as a scalable and practical tool for entanglement characterization in quantum optical systems.

AI.tldr: Deep learning framework reconstructs entanglement quasiprobabilities from incomplete local measurements, bypassing full state tomography, achieving 30× error reduction and experimental validation on photonic systems.
AI.motivation: Negativities in quasiprobability distributions are fundamental signatures of quantum nonclassicality, with entanglement quasiprobabilities providing necessary and sufficient entanglement criteria. However, conventional reconstruction requires full quantum state tomography, severely limiting scalability for practical applications.
AI.method: Proposes a deep-learning framework using a residual neural network that maps partial local projective measurement outcomes directly to high-fidelity entanglement quasiprobabilities, bypassing full state reconstruction.
AI.result: Numerical benchmarks up to three qubits show more than 30× reduction in reconstruction error compared with state-of-the-art tomographic methods. Experimental validation on photonic entangled states demonstrates reconstruction and entanglement detection with substantially reduced measurement resources.
AI.conclusion: Establishes machine-learning-assisted reconstruction of entanglement quasiprobabilities as a scalable and practical tool for entanglement characterization in quantum optical systems, overcoming traditional tomography limitations.

title: Inhomogeneous mass trap for dark-state polaritons in atomic media
summary: The generation of a trapping potential for dark-state polaritons in a two-dimensional electromagnetically induced transparency system is theoretically studied. We show that such a trap can arise from a spatially inhomogeneous effective mass of the dark-state polariton. Because this mass inhomogeneity can be engineered by tuning the parameters of the control fields, the motion, spatial profile, and coherent behavior of bound dark-state polaritons can be tailored accordingly. Our results enable spatial controls of optical information and provide a possible route toward realizing Bose-Einstein condensation of dark-state polaritons in a trapping potential.

AI.tldr: Theoretical study shows how to create trapping potentials for dark-state polaritons in 2D EIT systems using spatially inhomogeneous effective mass engineering via control field parameters.
AI.motivation: To enable spatial control of optical information and provide a pathway toward realizing Bose-Einstein condensation of dark-state polaritons in trapping potentials.
AI.method: Theoretical study of two-dimensional electromagnetically induced transparency systems, demonstrating that trapping potentials can arise from spatially inhomogeneous effective mass of dark-state polaritons engineered by tuning control field parameters.
AI.result: Shows that motion, spatial profile, and coherent behavior of bound dark-state polaritons can be tailored through engineered mass inhomogeneity, enabling spatial control of optical information.
AI.conclusion: The approach provides a possible route toward realizing Bose-Einstein condensation of dark-state polaritons in trapping potentials through parameter-engineered effective mass inhomogeneity.

title: Simulating Quantum Error Correction beyond Pauli Stochastic Errors
summary: Quantum error correction (QEC), the lynchpin of fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC), is designed and validated against well-behaved Pauli stochastic error models. But in real-world deployment, QEC protocols encounter a vast array of other errors -- coherent and non-Pauli errors -- whose impacts on quantum circuits are vastly different than those of stochastic Pauli errors. The impacts of these errors on QEC and FTQC protocols have been largely unpredictable to date due to exponential classical simulation cost. Here, we show how to accurately and efficiently model the effects of coherent and non-Pauli errors on FTQC, and we study the effects of such errors on syndrome extraction for surface and bivariate bicycle codes, and on magic state cultivation. Our analysis suggests that coherent error can shift fault-tolerance thresholds, increase the space-time cost of magic state cultivation, and can increase logical error rates by an order of magnitude compared to equivalent stochastic errors. These analyses are enabled by a new technique for mapping any Markovian circuit-level error model with sufficiently small error rates onto a detector error model (DEM) for an FTQC circuit. The resulting DEM enables Monte Carlo estimation of logical error rates and noise-adapted decoding, and its parameters can be analytically related to the underlying physical noise parameters to enable approximate strong simulation.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a technique to model coherent and non-Pauli errors in fault-tolerant quantum computing, enabling analysis of their impact on quantum error correction protocols through mapping to detector error models.
AI.motivation: Current quantum error correction protocols are designed for stochastic Pauli errors, but real-world deployment encounters coherent and non-Pauli errors whose impacts on fault-tolerant quantum computing are unpredictable due to exponential classical simulation costs.
AI.method: Develops a technique to map any Markovian circuit-level error model with sufficiently small error rates onto a detector error model for fault-tolerant quantum computing circuits, enabling Monte Carlo estimation of logical error rates and noise-adapted decoding.
AI.result: Coherent errors can shift fault-tolerance thresholds, increase space-time cost of magic state cultivation, and increase logical error rates by an order of magnitude compared to equivalent stochastic errors. The method enables accurate modeling of coherent and non-Pauli errors on surface and bivariate bicycle codes.
AI.conclusion: The developed technique provides an efficient way to model and analyze the effects of coherent and non-Pauli errors on fault-tolerant quantum computing, revealing significant performance impacts that differ substantially from stochastic Pauli error models.

title: Barren Plateaus Beyond Observable Concentration
summary: Parameterized quantum circuits (PQCs) are central to quantum machine learning and near-term quantum simulation, but their scalability is often hindered by barren plateaus (BPs), where gradients decay exponentially with system size. Prior explanations, including expressivity, entanglement, locality, and noise, are often presented in ways that conflate two distinct issues: concentration of the measured observable and loss of parameter sensitivity caused by circuit dynamics. We develop a unified statistical framework that separates these mechanisms. We show that several standard BP explanations, including locality- and entanglement-related effects, can be understood through a single phenomenon that we term observable concentration (OC). Importantly, we prove that avoiding OC is necessary but not sufficient for trainability. Beyond OC, we identify two distinct mid-circuit sources of gradient suppression. First, mid-circuit information loss occurs when parameter perturbations propagate into degrees of freedom that are inaccessible to the final measurement, yielding little or no response. Second, mid-circuit information scrambling occurs when local perturbations rapidly spread across the system and become effectively undetectable on the measured subsystem. We support our theory with explicit constructions and numerical evidence, including quantum convolutional neural network architectures that exhibit information-loss-induced barren plateaus despite the absence of observable concentration.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a unified statistical framework that separates observable concentration from mid-circuit gradient suppression mechanisms in parameterized quantum circuits, identifying two distinct sources of barren plateaus beyond observable concentration.
AI.motivation: Current explanations for barren plateaus in parameterized quantum circuits conflate two distinct issues: concentration of measured observables and loss of parameter sensitivity from circuit dynamics. A unified framework is needed to separate these mechanisms and better understand gradient suppression.
AI.method: Developed a unified statistical framework that separates observable concentration from mid-circuit gradient suppression. Identified two distinct mid-circuit sources: information loss (when parameter perturbations propagate into inaccessible degrees of freedom) and information scrambling (when local perturbations spread across the system). Supported with explicit constructions and numerical evidence.
AI.result: Showed that several standard barren plateau explanations can be understood through observable concentration alone, but avoiding observable concentration is necessary but not sufficient for trainability. Demonstrated quantum convolutional neural network architectures that exhibit information-loss-induced barren plateaus despite absence of observable concentration.
AI.conclusion: Barren plateaus in parameterized quantum circuits arise from distinct mechanisms: observable concentration and mid-circuit gradient suppression (information loss and information scrambling). This separation provides a clearer understanding of trainability limitations and suggests new approaches for designing scalable quantum circuits.

title: Gravitational Wave-Induced Scrambling Delay in SYK Wormhole Teleportation
comment: 18 + 7 pages, 9 Figures. To be submitted shortly to a Journal
summary: Traversable wormhole teleportation in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model links quantum channel integrity to black hole interior dynamics, using teleportation fidelity to probe holographic scrambling. We subject the SYK boundary to a gravitational-wave (GW)-inspired periodic Floquet deformation, mimicking a leading-order metric-strain perturbation from the JT-gravity dictionary. We characterize the channel response via exact numerical time evolution with disorder averaging at $βJ = 2$. The drive produces a coherent, frequency-selective fidelity suppression, yielding four main results: (i) two amplitude regimes separated near $\varepsilon \sim J$ (perturbative sensing vs.\ strong-drive); (ii) the channel acts as a low-pass filter, most sensitive at $ω\lesssim β^{-1}$ with monotone recovery above the thermal scale; (iii) an inspiral chirp drive delays the fidelity peak by $Δt_{\rm scr}^{(\rm fid)} = +0.11\, J^{-1}$, corroborated by an out-of-time-order correlator (OTOC) diagnostic ($Δt_{\rm scr}^{(\rm OTOC)} = +0.20\, J^{-1}$), establishing a genuine scrambling delay; and (iv) the effects persist across $N \in \{10, 12, 14, 16\}$ Majorana modes, indicating no systematic finite-size suppression. These results establish that holographic teleportation channels degrade gracefully under GW-inspired boundary deformations, with direct implications for near-term quantum processor implementations of traversable wormholes.

AI.tldr: Traversable wormhole teleportation in SYK model shows gravitational-wave-inspired boundary deformations cause frequency-selective fidelity suppression, acting as low-pass filter with scrambling delay, persisting across system sizes.
AI.motivation: To understand how quantum channel integrity in holographic teleportation responds to gravitational-wave-inspired boundary deformations, linking quantum information processing to black hole interior dynamics and probing holographic scrambling.
AI.method: Apply GW-inspired periodic Floquet deformation to SYK boundary (mimicking metric-strain perturbation from JT-gravity dictionary), characterize channel response via exact numerical time evolution with disorder averaging at βJ = 2, using teleportation fidelity and OTOC diagnostics across N ∈ {10, 12, 14, 16} Majorana modes.
AI.result: Four main findings: (i) Two amplitude regimes separated near ε ∼ J; (ii) Channel acts as low-pass filter, most sensitive at ω ≲ β⁻¹ with monotone recovery above thermal scale; (iii) Inspiral chirp drive delays fidelity peak by Δtₛᶜʳ⁽ᶠⁱᵈ⁾ = +0.11 J⁻¹, corroborated by OTOC diagnostic (Δtₛᶜʳ⁽ᴼᵀᴼᶜ⁾ = +0.20 J⁻¹); (iv) Effects persist across system sizes with no finite-size suppression.
AI.conclusion: Holographic teleportation channels degrade gracefully under GW-inspired boundary deformations, establishing that quantum channels remain robust to such perturbations with implications for near-term quantum processor implementations of traversable wormholes.

title: End-to-End QGAN-Based Image Synthesis via Neural Noise Encoding and Intensity Calibration
summary: Quantum Generative Adversarial Networks (QGANs) offer a promising path for learning data distributions on near-term quantum devices. However, existing QGANs for image synthesis avoid direct full-image generation, relying on classical post-processing or patch-based methods. These approaches dilute the quantum generator's role and struggle to capture global image semantics. To address this, we propose ReQGAN, an end-to-end framework that synthesizes an entire N=2^D-pixel image using a single D-qubit quantum circuit. ReQGAN overcomes two fundamental bottlenecks hindering direct pixel generation: (1) the rigid classical-to-quantum noise interface and (2) the output mismatch between normalized quantum statistics and the desired pixel-intensity space. We introduce a learnable Neural Noise Encoder for adaptive state preparation and a differentiable Intensity Calibration module to map measurements to a stable, visually meaningful pixel domain. Experiments on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST demonstrate that ReQGAN achieves stable training and effective image synthesis under stringent qubit budgets, with ablation studies verifying the contribution of each component.

AI.tldr: ReQGAN is an end-to-end quantum GAN framework that directly synthesizes full images using minimal qubits, overcoming interface and output mapping bottlenecks through learnable noise encoding and intensity calibration.
AI.motivation: Existing QGANs for image synthesis avoid direct full-image generation, relying on classical post-processing or patch-based methods that dilute the quantum generator's role and struggle to capture global image semantics. There's a need for true end-to-end quantum image synthesis with minimal qubit requirements.
AI.method: ReQGAN uses a single D-qubit quantum circuit to synthesize entire N=2^D-pixel images. It introduces two key components: (1) a learnable Neural Noise Encoder for adaptive state preparation to overcome rigid classical-to-quantum noise interface limitations, and (2) a differentiable Intensity Calibration module to map quantum measurement statistics to stable, visually meaningful pixel intensities.
AI.result: Experiments on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST demonstrate that ReQGAN achieves stable training and effective image synthesis under stringent qubit budgets. Ablation studies verify the contribution of each proposed component to the framework's success.
AI.conclusion: ReQGAN represents a significant advancement in quantum image synthesis by enabling direct full-image generation with minimal qubit resources, overcoming fundamental bottlenecks in classical-to-quantum interface design and output space mapping.

title: High-threshold magic state distillation with quantum quadratic residue codes
summary: We present applications of quantum quadratic residue codes in magic state distillation. This includes showing that existing codes which are known to distill magic states, like the $5$-qubit perfect code, the $7$-qubit Steane code, and the $11$-qutrit and $23$-qubit Golay codes, are equivalent to certain quantum quadratic residue codes. We also present new examples of quantum quadratic residue codes that distill qubit $T$ states and qutrit Strange states with high thresholds, and we show that there are infinitely many quantum quadratic residue codes that distill $T$ states with a non-trivial threshold. All of these codes, including the codes with the highest currently known thresholds for $T$ state and Strange state distillation, are unified under the umbrella of quantum quadratic residue codes.

AI.tldr: Quantum quadratic residue codes unify known magic state distillation codes and provide new high-threshold examples for qubit T states and qutrit Strange states.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that quantum quadratic residue codes provide a unifying framework for magic state distillation, showing that existing high-performance codes (5-qubit perfect code, 7-qubit Steane code, 11-qutrit and 23-qubit Golay codes) are special cases, and to discover new high-threshold distillation codes within this framework.
AI.method: Apply quantum quadratic residue codes to magic state distillation, showing equivalence between known distillation codes and specific quantum quadratic residue codes, and construct new quantum quadratic residue codes for qubit T states and qutrit Strange states.
AI.result: Established that existing high-performance magic state distillation codes are equivalent to quantum quadratic residue codes; discovered new quantum quadratic residue codes that distill qubit T states and qutrit Strange states with high thresholds; proved existence of infinitely many quantum quadratic residue codes that distill T states with non-trivial thresholds.
AI.conclusion: Quantum quadratic residue codes provide a comprehensive framework unifying all known high-threshold magic state distillation codes, including those with the highest currently known thresholds for T state and Strange state distillation, demonstrating their fundamental role in fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Distribution of fidelity zeros in two-band topological models
summary: We investigate the distribution of fidelity zeros in two-band topological models by extending the phase transition driving parameter into the complex plane. Within the biorthogonal formulation, we unveil that fidelity zeros are related to momentum modes for which the real part of the energy gap vanishes. Guided by this relation, we analyze the Kitaev chain, the Haldane model, and the Qi-Wu-Zhang (QWZ) model. In finite-size systems the zeros form discrete lines parallel to the imaginary axis, while in the thermodynamic limit they accumulate into extended regions in the complex parameter plane. For the Kitaev and Haldane models, the accessible interval of the real part of the complexified parameter is bounded by the critical points of the corresponding topological transitions. For the QWZ model, the transitions at $u = \pm2$ are identified in the same way, whereas the critical point at $u = 0$ is signaled by fidelity zeros crossing the real axis. These results extend the fidelity-zero framework to topological quantum phase transitions and clarify how critical information is encoded in complexified parameter space.

AI.tldr: Fidelity zeros in two-band topological models reveal critical points when parameters are extended to complex plane, with zeros forming discrete lines in finite systems and extended regions in thermodynamic limit.
AI.motivation: To understand how fidelity zeros (points where quantum fidelity vanishes) relate to topological phase transitions in two-band models by extending real parameters into the complex plane within biorthogonal formulation.
AI.method: Extend phase transition driving parameters into complex plane, use biorthogonal formulation to relate fidelity zeros to momentum modes with vanishing real part of energy gap, analyze Kitaev chain, Haldane model, and QWZ model.
AI.result: Fidelity zeros form discrete lines parallel to imaginary axis in finite systems, accumulate into extended regions in thermodynamic limit. For Kitaev and Haldane models, accessible interval of real part bounded by topological transition critical points. For QWZ model, transitions at u=±2 identified similarly, while u=0 transition signaled by fidelity zeros crossing real axis.
AI.conclusion: Fidelity-zero framework extends to topological quantum phase transitions, revealing how critical information is encoded in complexified parameter space through relationships between zeros and momentum modes with vanishing real energy gaps.

title: Schrödinger Bridges via the Hacking of Bayesian Priors in Classical and Quantum Regimes
comment: 12 pages (main text, 23 pages total with appendix), 8 Figures,
summary: Bayes' rule is widely regarded as the canonical prescription for belief updating. We show, however, that one can arbitrarily preserve pre-specified beliefs while appearing to perform Bayesian updates via "prior hacking": engineering a reference prior distribution such that, for a fixed channel and evidence, the update matches a chosen target distribution. We prove that this is generically possible in both classical and quantum settings whenever Bayesian inversions are well-defined (with the Petz recovery map as the quantum analogue to Bayes' rule), and provide constructive algorithms for doing so. We further establish a duality between prior hacking and Schrödinger bridge problems (a key object in statistical physics with applications in generative modelling), yielding in the quantum setting a unique, inference-consistent selection among candidate bridges. This formally establishes the Bayes-like updating that Schrödinger bridges are performing with respect to the process as opposed to the reference prior, both in classical and quantum settings.

AI.tldr: Prior hacking enables arbitrary belief preservation while appearing Bayesian by engineering reference priors, with connections to Schrödinger bridges in both classical and quantum settings.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that Bayesian updating can be manipulated to preserve pre-specified beliefs while maintaining the appearance of proper Bayesian inference, challenging the canonical status of Bayes' rule as the definitive prescription for belief updating.
AI.method: Develop "prior hacking" techniques that engineer reference prior distributions such that Bayesian updates match chosen target distributions for fixed channels and evidence, with constructive algorithms for both classical and quantum settings using Petz recovery maps as quantum analogues to Bayes' rule.
AI.result: Proves prior hacking is generically possible whenever Bayesian inversions are well-defined, establishes duality between prior hacking and Schrödinger bridge problems, and yields a unique inference-consistent selection among candidate bridges in quantum settings.
AI.conclusion: Formally establishes that Schrödinger bridges perform Bayes-like updating with respect to the process rather than reference priors, revealing fundamental limitations in treating Bayesian updating as canonical while providing new connections between inference theory and statistical physics.

title: On-chip Parametric Amplification in a Double Quantum Dots Circuit
summary: In microwave-based quantum circuits, including double quantum dots (DQDs), superconducting qubits and spin qubits, parametric amplifiers are indispensable in achieving high-fidelity qubit readouts. Despite its importance, the application of parametric amplifiers is hampered by several challenges, such as high insertion losses, constrained tunability, and a pronounced vulnerability to magnetic fields. Here, we demonstrate an on-site single-atom parametric amplifier (SAPA) within a reconfigurable quantum circuit, which consists of a superconducting microwave cavity and two GaAs gate-defined DQDs. Leveraging the inherent nonlinearity of the DQD, a parametric gain exceeding 11 dB is achieved. This gain contributes to enhance the qubit readout, as evidenced by exceeding two times improvement in the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) when employing the DQD-based amplifier for reading out another DQD. Our work not only presents a versatile experimental platform with enhanced readout capabilities in quantum computing, but also introduces alternative choices of parametric amplifiers for a variety of microwave-based quantum circuits.

AI.tldr: Demonstration of an on-site single-atom parametric amplifier (SAPA) using double quantum dots in a superconducting microwave cavity, achieving >11 dB gain and >2× SNR improvement for qubit readout.
AI.motivation: Parametric amplifiers are essential for high-fidelity qubit readout in microwave-based quantum circuits, but current implementations face challenges including high insertion losses, limited tunability, and sensitivity to magnetic fields.
AI.method: Developed a reconfigurable quantum circuit combining a superconducting microwave cavity with two GaAs gate-defined double quantum dots (DQDs), leveraging the inherent nonlinearity of DQDs to create a single-atom parametric amplifier.
AI.result: Achieved parametric gain exceeding 11 dB, demonstrated >2× improvement in signal-to-noise ratio when using the DQD-based amplifier to read out another DQD, providing enhanced readout capabilities.
AI.conclusion: The work presents a versatile experimental platform with improved readout capabilities for quantum computing and introduces alternative parametric amplifier options for various microwave-based quantum circuits.

title: Teleporting an unknown qutrit state via a 2-qudit entangled channel
summary: We propose a quantum teleportation scheme for transmitting a single qutrit state by adopting a 2-qudit entangled state as the quantum channel. The measurement basis for Alice has been carefully and systematically constructed, which is essential for the successful implementation of the teleportation protocol. Based on Alice's measurement outcomes, we design the corresponding collective unitary transformations to be performed by Bob on an auxiliary qubit and information particle. After implementing the collective unitary transformation, Bob performs a von Neumann measurement on the auxiliary qubit. The single qutrit state is then teleported to the distant receiver Bob with a finite success probability. We obtain the achievable success probabilities of the proposed teleportation scheme for different quantum channels. The obtained results not only enrich the theory of quantum teleportation over high-dimensional entangled channels but also provide a novel and feasible approach to implementing qutrit teleportation.

AI.tldr: Quantum teleportation scheme for single qutrit states using 2-qudit entangled channels with systematic measurement basis construction and collective unitary transformations.
AI.motivation: To develop a practical quantum teleportation protocol for high-dimensional quantum states (qutrits) using entangled quantum channels, enriching teleportation theory and providing feasible implementation approaches.
AI.method: Uses 2-qudit entangled state as quantum channel; constructs systematic measurement basis for Alice; designs collective unitary transformations for Bob based on measurement outcomes; implements von Neumann measurement on auxiliary qubit.
AI.result: Achieves finite success probability for teleporting single qutrit states; obtains success probabilities for different quantum channels; demonstrates feasibility of qutrit teleportation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed scheme enriches quantum teleportation theory for high-dimensional entangled channels and provides a novel, feasible approach to implementing qutrit teleportation with finite success probabilities.

title: A simple understanding of quantum electrodynamics using Bohmian trajectories: detecting non-ontic photons
summary: The use of Bohmian mechanics as a practical tool for modeling non-relativistic quantum phenomena of matter provides clear evidence of its success, not only as a way to interpret the foundations of quantum mechanics, but also as a computational framework. In the literature, it is frequently argued that such a realistic view-based on deterministic trajectories cannot account for phenomena involving the "creation" and "annihilation" of photons. In this paper, by revisiting and rehabilitating earlier proposals, we show how quantum optics can be modeled using Bohmian trajectories for electrons in physical space, together with well-defined electromagnetic fields evolving in time. By paying special attention to an experiment demonstrating partition noise for photons, and to how the Born rule emerges in this context, the paper pursues two main goals. First, it vindicates the pedagogical use of this simple Bohmian framework to compute, understand, and visualize quantum electrodynamics phenomena. Second, given that measurements are ultimately indicated on matter pointers, it clarifies what it means to measure photon or electromagnetic-field properties, even when they are considered non-ontic elements.

AI.tldr: Bohmian mechanics can model quantum optics phenomena including photon creation/annihilation using electron trajectories and electromagnetic fields, addressing criticisms about its applicability to quantum electrodynamics.
AI.motivation: To counter the frequent argument that Bohmian mechanics cannot account for photon creation/annihilation phenomena, and to demonstrate its practical utility as both an interpretational framework and computational tool for quantum electrodynamics.
AI.method: Revisiting and rehabilitating earlier proposals to model quantum optics using Bohmian trajectories for electrons in physical space together with well-defined electromagnetic fields evolving in time, with special attention to partition noise experiments and emergence of the Born rule.
AI.result: Shows that Bohmian mechanics can successfully model quantum optics phenomena, including photon-related effects, using a framework where electromagnetic fields are treated as non-ontic elements while measurements are indicated on matter pointers.
AI.conclusion: The paper vindicates the pedagogical use of Bohmian mechanics for computing, understanding, and visualizing QED phenomena, and clarifies what it means to measure photon properties even when they are considered non-ontic elements.

title: Comment on "Association between quantum paradoxes based on weak values and a realistic interpretation of quantum measurements"
summary: In their paper (arXiv:2402.09879), Aredes and Saldanha analyze several paradoxes related to weak values and present a "general argument" that aims to show that "realistic interpretations ...of weak values lead to inconsistencies". Although we agree with the identified inconsistencies for the specific weak values analyzed there, in this Comment we demonstrate that the origin of these inconsistencies is not their general argument, which is formally incorrect. We use Bohmian mechanics as a counterexample to confirm that their conclusions are not valid for all weak values and quantum theories. In particular, we show that weak values postselected in position can in fact be interpreted within Bohmian mechanics as properties of quantum systems, detached from any measuring devices, in a consistent and meaningful way.

AI.tldr: The authors refute a general argument against realistic interpretations of weak values by showing it's formally incorrect, using Bohmian mechanics as a counterexample where position-postselected weak values can be consistently interpreted as system properties.
AI.motivation: To challenge Aredes and Saldanha's claim that realistic interpretations of weak values inevitably lead to inconsistencies, demonstrating their general argument is flawed and not universally applicable.
AI.method: The authors analyze the formal correctness of Aredes and Saldanha's general argument and use Bohmian mechanics as a counterexample, specifically examining weak values postselected in position within this theoretical framework.
AI.result: The general argument against realistic interpretations of weak values is shown to be formally incorrect. Bohmian mechanics provides a consistent framework where position-postselected weak values can be meaningfully interpreted as intrinsic properties of quantum systems, independent of measurement devices.
AI.conclusion: Aredes and Saldanha's general argument fails; realistic interpretations of weak values are not universally inconsistent. Bohmian mechanics demonstrates that at least some weak values (position-postselected) can be consistently interpreted as genuine system properties.

title: A generalized framework for quantum subspace diagonalization
summary: We present a framework for computing the solution to Hamiltonian eigenproblems in a subspace defined by bit-strings sampled from a quantum computer. Hamiltonians are represented using an extended alphabet that includes projection and ladder operators, yielding a unified solution method for qubit and fermionic systems. Operators are grouped and sorted so that only non-zero terms are evaluated and a minimal number of subspace lookup operations are performed. Bit-strings are expressed using bit-sets to reduce memory consumption and allow for evaluating operators with no intrinsic limitation on the number of qubits. Subspaces defined over bit-sets are stored in a hash map format that allows for efficient indexing and lookup operations. Our method can be used to directly construct sparse matrix representations or obtain matrix-free solutions. Users are free to utilize these in their eigensolver of choice. We show the benefits of our framework by computing the ground-state solution to examples from condensed matter physics and quantum chemistry with less memory and runtime compared to existing techniques, in some cases by an order of magnitude or more. This work provides a flexible interface for performant quantum-classical eigensolutions for candidate quantum advantage applications.

AI.tldr: A framework for solving Hamiltonian eigenproblems using quantum computer-sampled bit-strings with efficient subspace representation and operator evaluation.
AI.motivation: To develop a flexible, memory-efficient framework for quantum-classical eigensolutions that can handle large Hamiltonians and reduce computational costs compared to existing techniques.
AI.method: Represent Hamiltonians with extended alphabet including projection/ladder operators, group/sort operators to evaluate only non-zero terms, use bit-sets for memory-efficient bit-string representation, store subspaces in hash maps for efficient lookup, and enable both sparse matrix construction and matrix-free solutions.
AI.result: Demonstrated reduced memory and runtime for ground-state solutions in condensed matter physics and quantum chemistry examples, achieving up to order-of-magnitude improvements over existing techniques.
AI.conclusion: Provides a flexible, performant interface for quantum-classical eigensolutions suitable for quantum advantage applications, with significant efficiency gains in memory and computational time.

title: Simulating Supersymmetric Quantum Mechanics Using Variational Quantum Algorithms
comment: 10 pages, 2 figures, Contribution to the 42nd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (LATTICE2025)
summary: The study of spontaneous supersymmetry breaking (SSB) on the lattice is obstructed by a severe sign problem. Quantum computing provides a promising alternative approach. In particular, properties of supersymmetry relate SSB to the ground-state energy, which can be probed using hybrid quantum--classical algorithms such as the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). In this work we present VQE analyses for supersymmetric quantum mechanics with various superpotentials. A key new feature is an adaptive ansatz construction algorithm that reduces the number of variational parameters within our ansätze. This lowers the resource burden on both the classical optimizer and the noisy quantum processor, thereby improving the feasibility of these calculations in the NISQ era. Additionally, we present preliminary VQE results obtained from real IBM quantum devices, highlighting accuracy, resource constraints, and computational cost, both with and without the application of error mitigation techniques.

AI.tldr: VQE analysis of supersymmetric quantum mechanics with adaptive ansatz construction to reduce variational parameters, enabling NISQ-era feasibility and demonstrating results on IBM quantum devices.
AI.motivation: Studying spontaneous supersymmetry breaking on classical computers faces severe sign problems, making quantum computing a promising alternative. Supersymmetry properties relate SSB to ground-state energy, which can be probed using hybrid quantum-classical algorithms like VQE.
AI.method: VQE analyses for supersymmetric quantum mechanics with various superpotentials, featuring an adaptive ansatz construction algorithm that reduces the number of variational parameters. This lowers resource burden on both classical optimizer and noisy quantum processor. Includes preliminary VQE results from real IBM quantum devices with and without error mitigation techniques.
AI.result: The adaptive ansatz construction reduces variational parameters, improving feasibility in the NISQ era. Preliminary results from IBM quantum devices highlight accuracy, resource constraints, and computational cost, demonstrating the approach's viability with error mitigation techniques.
AI.conclusion: VQE with adaptive ansatz construction provides a viable approach for studying supersymmetric quantum mechanics on NISQ devices, overcoming classical sign problems and reducing resource requirements while maintaining accuracy through error mitigation.

title: A Flexible GKP-State-Embedded Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation Configuration Based on a Three-Dimensional Cluster State
summary: The integration of diverse quantum resources and the exploitation of more degrees of freedom provide key operational flexibility for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation. In this work, we propose a flexible Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill-state-embedded fault-tolerant quantum computation architecture based on a three-dimensional cluster state constructed in polarization, frequency, and orbital angular momentum domains. Specifically, we design optical entanglement generators to produce three diverse entangled pairs, and subsequently construct a three-dimensional cluster state via a beam-splitter network with several time delays. Furthermore, we present a partially squeezed surface-GKP code to achieve fault-tolerant quantum computation and ultimately find the optimal choice of implementing the squeezing gate to give the best fault-tolerant performance (the fault-tolerant squeezing threshold is 11.5 dB). Our scheme is flexible, scalable, and experimentally feasible, providing versatile options for future optical fault-tolerant quantum computation architecture.

AI.tldr: A flexible fault-tolerant quantum computation architecture using 3D cluster states in polarization, frequency, and orbital angular momentum domains with GKP states, achieving 11.5 dB squeezing threshold.
AI.motivation: To achieve universal fault-tolerant quantum computation by integrating diverse quantum resources and exploiting multiple degrees of freedom for operational flexibility.
AI.method: Proposes a 3D cluster state architecture constructed in polarization, frequency, and orbital angular momentum domains using optical entanglement generators and beam-splitter networks with time delays. Implements a partially squeezed surface-GKP code for fault tolerance.
AI.result: Achieves fault-tolerant quantum computation with optimal squeezing gate implementation, obtaining a fault-tolerant squeezing threshold of 11.5 dB.
AI.conclusion: The scheme is flexible, scalable, and experimentally feasible, providing versatile options for future optical fault-tolerant quantum computation architectures.

title: Comparing optical-microwave conversion and all-microwave control schemes for a transmon qubit
summary: We report a comparative study on transmon qubit control using (i) conventional attenuated coaxial microwave line and (ii) an optical control system using modulated laser light delivered over telecommunications optical fiber to a photodiode located at the 1K stage of a dilution cryostat. During each experiment, we performed repeated measurements of the energy relaxation and coherence times of a transmon qubit using one of the control signal delivery methods. Each measurement run spanned 20 hours of measurement time and from these datasets we observe no measurable effect on coherence of the qubit compared to random coherence fluctuations. Our results open up the possibility of large scale integration of the optical qubit control system.

AI.tldr: Optical control of transmon qubits via fiber-delivered modulated laser light shows no measurable degradation of coherence compared to conventional microwave control, enabling scalable quantum system integration.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether optical control systems using fiber-delivered laser light can replace conventional microwave control lines for transmon qubits without compromising qubit coherence, enabling more scalable quantum computing architectures.
AI.method: Comparative study between two control methods: (1) conventional attenuated coaxial microwave line, and (2) optical control system using modulated laser light delivered via telecommunications optical fiber to a photodiode at the 1K stage of a dilution cryostat. Repeated measurements of energy relaxation and coherence times were performed for each method over 20-hour measurement runs.
AI.result: No measurable effect on qubit coherence was observed with optical control compared to conventional microwave control. The optical system performed equivalently within random coherence fluctuations observed in the datasets.
AI.conclusion: Optical control of transmon qubits is viable and opens possibilities for large-scale integration of optical qubit control systems in quantum computing architectures.

title: If Quantum Measurements Are Secretly Continuous Nonunitary Processes, Weak Measurements Can Detect It
summary: The standard approach to quantum measurements is to assume that they lead to effectively instantaneous collapse of the quantum state. However, if we assume that we are unable to enforce at what exact moment of time the measurement occurs due to a finite resolution of any time measurement device, at the level of the ensemble, the measurement would lead to an effectively nonunitary evolution involving a mixed state. Each individual ensemble member would face an instantaneous collapse at different moments of time. This process is completely indistinguishable from fundamental nonunitary evolution at the level of each individual ensemble member, within the framework of strong projective measurements. In this paper, we show that weak postselected measurements can distinguish these two types of evolution. An experimental protocol for determining the nature of quantum collapse is described, and the example of a hydrogen atom is analyzed in detail.

AI.tldr: Weak postselected measurements can distinguish between instantaneous quantum collapse and time-uncertain measurements, unlike strong projective measurements where they appear identical.
AI.motivation: Standard quantum measurement theory assumes instantaneous collapse, but practical time measurement limitations create ensemble-level mixed states indistinguishable from fundamental nonunitary evolution under strong projective measurements.
AI.method: Use weak postselected measurements to distinguish between instantaneous collapse and time-uncertain measurements, develop experimental protocol, and analyze hydrogen atom example.
AI.result: Weak measurements reveal differences between the two evolution types that strong projective measurements cannot detect, providing a method to determine the nature of quantum collapse.
AI.conclusion: Weak postselected measurements offer a novel approach to experimentally test whether quantum collapse is fundamentally instantaneous or appears so due to time measurement limitations.

title: Time-Multiplexed Distributed Quantum Sensing
summary: Quantum metrology enables parameter estimation beyond classical limits by exploiting nonclassical resources such as squeezing and entanglement. In distributed quantum sensing, Heisenberg scaling has been extended from $1/N^2$ to $1/(NM)^2$ through entanglement across both particles and spatial modes, where $N$ denotes the photon number and $M$ the number of spatially distributed modes. However, the overall sensitivity has remained limited to linear scaling with the number of measurement repetitions $R$. Here, we show that exploiting entanglement across temporal modes via time-domain multiplexing enables a scaling advantage with respect to $R$. As a result, the sensitivity can asymptotically approach simultaneous Heisenberg scaling in photons, spatial modes, and repetitions, yielding an overall sensitivity approaching $Δ^2 φ\propto 1/(NMR)^2$. Using the Bogoliubov transformation formalism, we prove the optimality of the protocol within the class of Gaussian states and show that the scaling is realizable via homodyne detection and maximum-likelihood estimation. We further show that the advantage persists under optical loss and propose an experimentally feasible loop-based photonic sensing scheme. Our results open a route to incorporating time-multiplexing techniques into quantum metrology.

AI.tldr: Quantum metrology achieves simultaneous Heisenberg scaling in photons, spatial modes, and measurement repetitions via temporal-mode entanglement and time-domain multiplexing, enabling sensitivity scaling as 1/(NMR)².
AI.motivation: Distributed quantum sensing has achieved Heisenberg scaling across particles and spatial modes (1/(NM)²), but overall sensitivity remains limited to linear scaling with measurement repetitions R. The authors aim to overcome this limitation by exploiting entanglement across temporal modes.
AI.method: The authors use time-domain multiplexing to create entanglement across temporal modes, enabling scaling advantage with respect to measurement repetitions. They employ Bogoliubov transformation formalism to prove protocol optimality within Gaussian states, and demonstrate implementation via homodyne detection and maximum-likelihood estimation.
AI.result: The protocol achieves simultaneous Heisenberg scaling in photons (N), spatial modes (M), and repetitions (R), yielding overall sensitivity scaling as Δ²φ ∝ 1/(NMR)². The advantage persists under optical loss, and an experimentally feasible loop-based photonic sensing scheme is proposed.
AI.conclusion: Exploiting entanglement across temporal modes via time-domain multiplexing enables unprecedented scaling advantages in quantum metrology, opening routes to incorporate time-multiplexing techniques for enhanced parameter estimation beyond previous limitations.

title: Quantum Advantage: a Tensor Network Perspective
summary: We review the recent quantum advantage experiments by IBM, D-Wave, and Google, focusing on cases where efficient classical simulations of the experiment were demonstrated or attempted using tensor network methods. We assess the strengths and limitations of these tensor network-based approaches and examine how the interplay between classical simulation and quantum hardware has advanced both fields. Our goal is to clarify what these results imply for the next generation of quantum advantage experiments. We identify regimes and system features that remain challenging for current tensor network approaches, and we outline directions where improved classical methods could further raise the standard for claiming quantum advantage. By analyzing this evolving competition, we aim to provide a clear view of where genuine, scalable quantum advantage is most likely to emerge.

AI.tldr: Review of quantum advantage experiments by IBM, D-Wave, and Google, analyzing classical tensor network simulations that challenged quantum claims, assessing limitations, and identifying future directions for genuine quantum advantage.
AI.motivation: To analyze recent quantum advantage experiments where classical tensor network simulations were used to challenge quantum claims, assess the interplay between classical simulation and quantum hardware, and clarify implications for next-generation quantum advantage experiments.
AI.method: Review and analysis of quantum advantage experiments from major companies (IBM, D-Wave, Google) with focus on cases where efficient classical simulations using tensor network methods were demonstrated or attempted. Assessment of strengths/limitations of tensor network approaches and examination of the competition between classical simulation and quantum hardware.
AI.result: Identified regimes and system features that remain challenging for current tensor network approaches, outlined directions where improved classical methods could further raise standards for claiming quantum advantage, and analyzed the evolving competition between classical and quantum approaches.
AI.conclusion: Provides a clear view of where genuine, scalable quantum advantage is most likely to emerge by analyzing the interplay between classical simulation advances and quantum hardware development, helping to establish more rigorous standards for future quantum advantage claims.

title: Certifying ergotropy under partial information
summary: Ergotropy, the maximum work extractable from a quantum system, is a central resource in quantum physics. Computing ergotropy is well established when the system state is fully known, but its estimation under partial information remains an open problem. Here we introduce a general certification framework that lower bounds ergotropy using only the expectation values of a limited set of arbitrary observables. The method naturally applies in the finite-statistics regime, yielding confidence-certified bounds that explicitly incorporate shot noise. We benchmark our approach on both synthetic data and experimental measurements from an IBM quantum processor. This establishes a robust and experimentally accessible tool for certifying extractable work in realistic quantum settings.

AI.tldr: Framework for certifying lower bounds on quantum ergotropy using limited observable measurements, applicable to finite-statistics scenarios with experimental validation.
AI.motivation: Ergotropy estimation under partial information remains an open problem despite established methods for fully known quantum states.
AI.method: General certification framework using expectation values of limited arbitrary observables, incorporating finite-statistics regime with shot noise.
AI.result: Benchmarked on synthetic data and IBM quantum processor experiments, establishing robust experimentally accessible certification tool.
AI.conclusion: Provides practical tool for certifying extractable work in realistic quantum settings with partial information.

title: Optimal and improved gate decompositions for accelerated classical simulation of near-Gaussian fermionic circuits
summary: Fermionic Gaussian circuits can be simulated efficiently on a classical computer, but become universal when supplemented with non-Gaussian operations. Similar to stabilizer circuits augmented with non-stabilizer resources, these non-Gaussian circuits can be simulated classically using rank- or extent-based methods. These methods decompose non-Gaussian states or operations into Gaussian ones, with runtimes that scale polynomially with measures of non-Gaussianity such as the rank and the extent -- quantities that typically grow exponentially with the number of non-Gaussian resources. Current fermionic rank- and extent-based simulators are limited to Gaussian circuits with magic-state injection. Extending them to mixed states and non-unitary channels has been hindered by the lack of known extent-optimized decompositions for physically relevant gates and noisy channels. In this work, we address this gap. First, we derive analytic decompositions for key non-Gaussian gates and channels, including decompositions for arbitrary two-qubit fermionic gates which are provably optimal for diagonal gates or those acting on Jordan-Wigner-adjacent qubit pairs. Second, we show that stochastic Pauli noise can reduce the effective extent of non-Gaussian rotation gates, but that fermionic magic is substantially more robust to such noise than stabilizer magic. Finally, we demonstrate how these decompositions can accelerate classical sampling from the output distribution of a quantum circuit. This involves a generalization of existing sparsification methods, previously limited to convex-unitary channels, to circuits involving intermediate measurements and feed-forward. Our decompositions also yield speedups for emulating noisy Pauli rotations with quasiprobability simulators in the large-angle/arbitrary-strength-noise and small-angle/low-noise parameter regimes.

AI.tldr: The paper develops analytic decompositions for fermionic non-Gaussian gates and channels, enabling efficient classical simulation of fermionic circuits with magic-state injection, measurements, and feed-forward operations.
AI.motivation: Current fermionic simulators are limited to Gaussian circuits with magic-state injection and cannot handle mixed states or non-unitary channels due to lack of extent-optimized decompositions for physically relevant gates and noisy channels.
AI.method: Derived analytic decompositions for key non-Gaussian gates and channels, including provably optimal decompositions for arbitrary two-qubit fermionic gates; analyzed noise effects on fermionic magic; generalized sparsification methods to circuits with measurements and feed-forward.
AI.result: Obtained optimal decompositions for diagonal gates and Jordan-Wigner-adjacent qubit pairs; showed fermionic magic is more robust to stochastic Pauli noise than stabilizer magic; demonstrated accelerated classical sampling and speedups for emulating noisy Pauli rotations.
AI.conclusion: The developed decompositions bridge the gap in fermionic simulation, enabling efficient classical simulation of broader classes of fermionic circuits with non-Gaussian resources, measurements, and noise.

title: Quantum and classical approaches to the optimization of highway platooning: the two-vehicle matching problem
summary: Aerodynamic drag reduction on highways through vehicle platooning is a well-known concept, but it has not yet seen systematic uptake, arguably because of significant technological and legislative obstacles. As a low-tech entry point to real multi-vehicle platooning, "Windbreaking-as-a-Service" (WaaS) was introduced recently. Here we use a QUBO formulation to study classical metaheuristics such as simulated annealing and tabu search, together with emerging quantum heuristics including quantum annealing and variants of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). These heuristic solvers do not guarantee optimality, but they traverse the same higher-order landscape using polynomial memory. They can also be parallelized aggressively, and efficient classical post-processing can be used in hybrid workflows to return only valid schedules. This paper therefore positions QUBO as a common language that allows heterogeneous classical, quantum, and hybrid solvers to address the optimization of highway platooning.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes using QUBO formulations to optimize highway vehicle platooning via Windbreaking-as-a-Service, enabling heterogeneous classical, quantum, and hybrid solvers to address the optimization problem.
AI.motivation: Vehicle platooning for aerodynamic drag reduction faces technological and legislative barriers; Windbreaking-as-a-Service offers a low-tech entry point, but requires efficient optimization methods that can leverage emerging quantum computing alongside classical approaches.
AI.method: Formulates the platooning optimization problem as QUBO (Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization), enabling application of classical metaheuristics (simulated annealing, tabu search) and quantum heuristics (quantum annealing, QAOA variants) with polynomial memory requirements and parallelization capabilities.
AI.result: QUBO serves as a common language allowing heterogeneous solvers to address highway platooning optimization, with heuristic approaches that traverse higher-order landscapes efficiently and can incorporate classical post-processing in hybrid workflows.
AI.conclusion: QUBO formulation provides a unifying framework for optimizing Windbreaking-as-a-Service platooning using diverse classical, quantum, and hybrid solvers, facilitating practical implementation despite heuristic nature of the approaches.

title: Cavity Control of Strongly Correlated Electrons Beyond Resonant Coupling
summary: Interfacing materials with electromagnetic cavities offers a route to modify equilibrium properties through structured vacuum fluctuations. The coupling of light with correlated electrons lacks a characteristic energy scale, making vacuum induced modifications of such systems inherently off-resonant and sensitive to the full photon mode structure. Here, we present a non-perturbative calculation of the cavity induced modification of the magnetic exchange interaction $J$ of the half-filled Hubbard model, including all cavity modes and with parameters determined from first principles. We show that the strength of the modification is controlled by a generalized Purcell factor, proportional to the frequency integrated photonic density of states. This result identifies polaritonic surface cavities as promising platforms to modify correlated systems, while standard Fabry-Pérot resonators produce negligible effects due to spectral weight cancellations upon integration. To perform the calculation, we develop a consistent quantization scheme for materials coupled to a dielectric substrate, in the Coulomb gauge, which reveals a competition between static Coulomb screening and dynamical effects arising from the vector potential. Including both effects is essential to obtain even qualitatively correct predictions. For a gold substrate the light-matter interactions lead to a net enhancement of $J$, whose magnitude is large enough to be observable in two-magnon Raman spectroscopy. Our framework establishes a concrete design principle linking cavity geometry to material response in the off-resonant regime, which will guide future experimental and theoretical explorations.

AI.tldr: Cavity-induced modification of magnetic exchange interactions in correlated electron systems via structured vacuum fluctuations, with a non-perturbative calculation showing enhancement controlled by Purcell factor.
AI.motivation: To understand how electromagnetic cavities can modify equilibrium properties of correlated electron systems through vacuum fluctuations, particularly for systems lacking characteristic energy scales where effects are inherently off-resonant and sensitive to full photon mode structure.
AI.method: Non-perturbative calculation of cavity-induced modification of magnetic exchange interaction J in half-filled Hubbard model, including all cavity modes with parameters from first principles. Developed consistent quantization scheme for materials coupled to dielectric substrates in Coulomb gauge, accounting for competition between static Coulomb screening and dynamical vector potential effects.
AI.result: Modification strength controlled by generalized Purcell factor proportional to frequency-integrated photonic density of states. Polaritonic surface cavities show promise for modifying correlated systems, while Fabry-Pérot resonators produce negligible effects due to spectral weight cancellations. For gold substrate, light-matter interactions lead to net enhancement of J observable in two-magnon Raman spectroscopy.
AI.conclusion: Establishes concrete design principle linking cavity geometry to material response in off-resonant regime, providing framework to guide future experimental and theoretical explorations of cavity-modified correlated electron systems.

title: Long Distance Daylight Drone-based Quantum Key Distribution under Relative Motion
summary: Low-altitude drones can serve as dynamic nodes apparently mitigating terrain-induced impacts for quantum networks. However, it is extremely hard to establish a sable quantum link in a drone-based dynamic platform, which requires centimeter-level positioning techniques and high-precision time synchronization technologies. In this paper, we develop a single-ended polarization adaptive correction technology at both the transmitting and receiving ends. Based on this, we present the world's first kilometer-scale drone-based QKD network, achieving an 1.2 km free-space QKD link with a secure key rate of 2.76 kbps, suitable for urban quantum network deployment. We validate the feasibility of QKD between dynamic drone and ground unmanned vehicle at a relative speed of 1 m/s over a distance of 100 m, attaining a secure key rate of 70.94 kbps. This work advances drone-based QKD from static demonstrations to practical dynamic network, boasting great development potential for an airborne quantum internet.

AI.tldr: First demonstration of kilometer-scale drone-based QKD network using single-ended polarization adaptive correction, achieving 1.2 km free-space QKD link with 2.76 kbps secure key rate and dynamic QKD between drone and ground vehicle at 1 m/s relative speed.
AI.motivation: Low-altitude drones can serve as dynamic nodes to mitigate terrain impacts for quantum networks, but establishing stable quantum links on drone platforms is extremely challenging due to requirements for centimeter-level positioning and high-precision time synchronization.
AI.method: Developed single-ended polarization adaptive correction technology at both transmitting and receiving ends, enabling stable quantum key distribution on dynamic drone platforms.
AI.result: Achieved world's first kilometer-scale drone-based QKD network: 1.2 km free-space QKD link with 2.76 kbps secure key rate suitable for urban deployment, and validated QKD between dynamic drone and ground unmanned vehicle at 1 m/s relative speed over 100 m distance with 70.94 kbps secure key rate.
AI.conclusion: This work advances drone-based QKD from static demonstrations to practical dynamic networks, demonstrating great development potential for an airborne quantum internet.

title: Dependence of Lindbladian spectral statistics on the integrability of no-jump Hamiltonians and the recycling terms
summary: Spectral statistics probe integrability versus chaos and have recently been extended to Markovian open quantum systems described by Lindbladians, whose quantum-trajectory unraveling decomposes the evolution into no-jump dynamics generated by an effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian and recycling jumps. In this work, we perform spectrum-statistics diagnostics for Lindbladians and their effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonians. We show that recycling processes, symmetry constraints, and the Liouville-space structure crucially shape the spectral correlations. In particular, we identify a family of spectrally separable Lindbladians whose spectra exhibit robust Poisson statistics, despite the effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian varying from regular to chaotic. Our work establishes a unified spectral-statistics characterization for Lindbladians and their associated effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonians, deepening our understanding of integrable and chaotic spectral properties in open many-body systems.

AI.tldr: Spectral statistics analysis of Lindbladians and their effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonians reveals how recycling processes, symmetries, and Liouville-space structure shape spectral correlations, identifying spectrally separable Lindbladians with robust Poisson statistics despite varying non-Hermitian Hamiltonian chaos.
AI.motivation: To extend spectral statistics diagnostics from closed quantum systems to open quantum systems described by Lindbladians, understanding how integrability versus chaos manifests in open quantum dynamics through spectral correlations of Lindbladians and their associated effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonians.
AI.method: Perform spectrum-statistics diagnostics for Lindbladians and their effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonians derived from quantum-trajectory unraveling, analyzing how recycling processes, symmetry constraints, and Liouville-space structure influence spectral correlations.
AI.result: Identified a family of spectrally separable Lindbladians whose spectra exhibit robust Poisson statistics, even when the effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian varies from regular to chaotic. Recycling processes, symmetries, and Liouville-space structure crucially shape spectral correlations.
AI.conclusion: Established a unified spectral-statistics characterization for Lindbladians and their associated effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonians, deepening understanding of integrable and chaotic spectral properties in open many-body quantum systems.

title: XCOM: Full Mesh Network Synchronization and Low-Latency Communication for QICK (Quantum Instrumentation Control Kit)
summary: Quantum computing experiments and testbeds with large qubit counts have until recently been a privilege afforded only to large companies or quantum technologies where scaling to hundreds or thousands of qubits does not require a substantial increase in quantum control hardware (neutral atoms, trapped ions, or spin defects). Superconducting and spin qubit testbeds critically depend on scaling their control systems beyond what a single electronics board can provide. Multi-board control systems combining RF, fast DC control, bias, and readout require precise synchronization and communication across many hardware and firmware components. To address this, we present XCOM, a network that synchronizes QICK boards and the absolute clocks governing quantum program execution to within 100 ps, free of drift and loss of lock. XCOM also provides deterministic, all-to-all simultaneous data communication with latency below 185 ns. Like QICK itself, XCOM is compatible with a broad range of qubit technologies and is designed to scale to large systems.

AI.tldr: XCOM is a synchronization network for multi-board quantum control systems that provides sub-100 ps synchronization and sub-185 ns deterministic communication for scaling superconducting and spin qubit testbeds.
AI.motivation: Superconducting and spin qubit testbeds require scaling control systems beyond single-board capabilities, but multi-board systems need precise synchronization and communication across hardware/firmware components, which existing solutions lack.
AI.method: Developed XCOM network that synchronizes QICK boards and absolute clocks governing quantum program execution, achieving drift-free synchronization within 100 ps and providing deterministic all-to-all simultaneous data communication with latency below 185 ns.
AI.result: XCOM achieves synchronization within 100 ps (drift-free, no loss of lock) and deterministic all-to-all communication with latency below 185 ns, compatible with various qubit technologies and designed for large-scale systems.
AI.conclusion: XCOM addresses critical synchronization and communication challenges in scaling multi-board quantum control systems, enabling large-scale superconducting and spin qubit testbeds that were previously limited to single-board systems or other quantum technologies.

title: End-to-End Simulation of Chemical Dynamics on a Quantum Computer
summary: Simulations of chemical dynamics are a powerful means for understanding chemistry. However, classical computers struggle to simulate many chemical processes, especially non-adiabatic ones, where the Born-Oppenheimer approximation breaks down. Quantum computers could simulate quantum-chemical dynamics more efficiently than classical computers, but there is currently no complete quantum algorithm for calculating dynamical observables to within a known error. Here, we develop an efficient, end-to-end quantum algorithm for simulating chemical dynamics that avoids all uncontrolled approximations (including the Born-Oppenheimer approximation) and whose error is bounded subject to mild assumptions. To do so, we treat the nuclei and the electrons on an equal footing and simulate the full molecular wavefunction on a momentum-space grid in first quantization, including all algorithmic steps: initial-state preparation, time evolution using qubitization, and measurement of chemical observables such as reaction yields and rates. Our work gives the first algorithm for quantum simulation of chemistry whose end-to-end complexity achieves sublinear scaling in the size of the grid. We achieve this by developing an exponentially faster method for initial-state-preparation. Photochemistry is a likely early application of our algorithm and we estimate resources required for end-to-end simulations of non-adiabatic dynamics of atmospherically important molecules. Classically intractable photochemical computations could be performed using resources comparable to those required for other chemical applications of quantum computing.

AI.tldr: Quantum algorithm for simulating chemical dynamics with bounded error and sublinear scaling, treating nuclei and electrons equally without Born-Oppenheimer approximation.
AI.motivation: Classical computers struggle with non-adiabatic chemical dynamics where Born-Oppenheimer approximation breaks down; quantum computers could simulate quantum-chemical dynamics more efficiently but lack complete algorithms with known error bounds.
AI.method: Treat nuclei and electrons equally on momentum-space grid in first quantization; includes initial-state preparation, time evolution using qubitization, and measurement of observables; develops exponentially faster initial-state-preparation method.
AI.result: First quantum algorithm for chemistry simulation with sublinear scaling in grid size; provides resource estimates for photochemical applications; enables classically intractable computations with comparable resources to other quantum chemistry applications.
AI.conclusion: Complete quantum algorithm for chemical dynamics simulation with bounded error and efficient scaling, enabling practical simulation of non-adiabatic processes like photochemistry on quantum computers.

title: Multiparameter quantum estimation and Stirling Engine Performance in a Gravitational Cat State System
summary: We investigate the multiparameter quantum estimation and quantum thermodynamics properties of a gravitational cat state (gravcat) system composed of two interacting massive particles confined in double-well potentials. The system is described by an effective Hamiltonian involving the energy splitting parameter $ω$ and the gravitational coupling strength $γ$, while the interaction with a thermal environment is modeled through a Gibbs thermal state. Within the framework of quantum parameter estimation theory, we employ the quantum Fisher information matrix (QFIM) to analyze the precision limits for estimating the three fundamental parameters of the model, namely the gravitational coupling $γ$, the energy splitting $ω$, and the temperature $T$. Utilizing the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) formalism within the QFIM framework, we derive the analytical expressions of the estimation bounds and evaluate the corresponding minimal variances associated with the quantum Cramér-Rao bound. Both simultaneous and individual estimation strategies are investigated, and their performances are compared in different parameter regimes. Our results reveal the existence of optimal estimation regions where the precision is significantly enhanced and show that the relative efficiency of the estimation schemes strongly depends on the interaction strength, the energy gap, and the thermal environment. In addition, the thermodynamic behavior of the system is analyzed within the framework of a quantum Stirling cycle. The internal energy, entropy, heat exchanges, and work production are examined, allowing us to evaluate the efficiency of the gravcat-based quantum heat engine. The obtained results highlight the interplay between quantum metrology and quantum thermodynamics.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates quantum estimation and thermodynamics of a gravitational cat state system, analyzing precision limits for parameter estimation via quantum Fisher information and examining thermodynamic properties through a quantum Stirling cycle.
AI.motivation: To explore the interplay between quantum metrology and quantum thermodynamics in a gravitational cat state system, specifically examining how quantum parameter estimation precision relates to thermodynamic properties in a system of interacting massive particles in double-well potentials.
AI.method: Uses quantum Fisher information matrix (QFIM) with symmetric logarithmic derivative formalism to derive analytical expressions for estimation bounds (Cramér-Rao bound) for parameters γ (gravitational coupling), ω (energy splitting), and T (temperature). Models system-environment interaction via Gibbs thermal state and analyzes thermodynamic behavior through quantum Stirling cycle calculations.
AI.result: Reveals optimal estimation regions with enhanced precision, shows dependence of estimation efficiency on interaction strength, energy gap, and thermal environment. Demonstrates interplay between quantum metrology and thermodynamics in the gravcat system, with both simultaneous and individual estimation strategies showing different performances in various parameter regimes.
AI.conclusion: The study successfully connects quantum parameter estimation theory with quantum thermodynamics in gravitational cat state systems, showing how estimation precision and thermodynamic efficiency are interrelated and depend on system parameters, providing insights for quantum metrology and quantum heat engine applications.

title: Exact Law of Quantum Reversibility under Gaussian Pure Loss
comment: arXiv admin note: text overlap with arXiv:2603.06488
summary: Classical reverse diffusion is generated by changing the drift at fixed noise. We show that the quantum version of this principle obeys an exact law with a sharp phase boundary. For Gaussian pure-loss dynamics -- the canonical model of continuous-variable decoherence in optical attenuation channels, squeezed-light interferometric sensing, and superconducting bosonic architectures -- complete positivity, the requirement that the dynamics remain physical even for systems entangled with an ancilla, creates an exact phase boundary at which the minimum reverse cost vanishes, fixes the reverse-noise budget on both sides, and makes pure nonclassical targets dynamically singular. The minimum reverse cost vanishes exactly at a critical squeezing-to-thermal ratio and is strictly positive away from it, with a sharp asymmetry: below the boundary, standard reverse prescriptions such as the fixed-diffusion Bayes reverse remain feasible at mild cost; above it, these prescriptions become infeasible, the covariance-aligned generator remains CP-feasible and uniquely optimal, and the cost can be severe.
